definition.internallyExhausted: Every admissible route using current corpus inputs ends in a derivation, a bounded no-go, a unique smallest resolving calculation, or an explicit external-input boundary.
notSufficient: synthetic effect without a microscopic coefficient

blockers.firstMissingDatum: A declared compactification with oriented defect embedding and complete charged spectrum.
blockers.smallestResolvingCalculation: Reduce one specified compact charge-three Higgs action on the declared defect and derive the BF level, orientation, boundary terms and gapped charged modes.
blockers.falsifier: The reduction is noncompact, gauge anomalous, leaves an unintended gapless charged mode, or fails to produce the level-three sector.
blockers.externalInputBoundary: A complete ultraviolet or mesoscopic defect action and its boundary conditions.

blockers.firstMissingDatum: The selected vacuum and complete gauge-fixed quadratic action with coefficients and operator domains.
blockers.smallestResolvingCalculation: Compute the physical cohomology, pole masses and residues of one fully specified candidate action.
blockers.falsifier: One unavoidable negative-norm state, negative physical residue, unbounded domain, or unremoved second-time mode.
blockers.conditionalWork: Sectorwise Hessian inequalities and boundary-domain tests.
blockers.externalInputBoundary: Numerical coefficients, potential, gauge fixing and boundary domains.

blockers.firstMissingDatum: A physically sourced transforming asymmetry or history-bearing selector.
blockers.smallestResolvingCalculation: Instantiate one selector tuple, derive its selected chiral module, and compute anomalies and a nonzero CP-odd invariant.
blockers.falsifier: The selector is constructed only from invariant input, leaves mirrors, violates anomaly cancellation, or forces every CP-odd invariant to zero.
blockers.conditionalWork: Broken, twisted, boundary, index and history-dependent selector models.
blockers.externalInputBoundary: The physical origin and distribution of the asymmetric datum.

blockers.firstMissingDatum: A completed renormalized action and contact/improvement prescription.
blockers.smallestResolvingCalculation: Metric variation plus the renormalized Ward-identity audit for the fixed action and probes.
blockers.falsifier: No conserved gauge-consistent stress operator exists after allowed improvement and contact terms.
blockers.conditionalWork: Classical stress tensor and counterterm basis.
blockers.externalInputBoundary: Renormalization scheme and physical probe definition.

blockers.firstMissingDatum: A positive selected spectrum with a defined heavy/light split.
blockers.smallestResolvingCalculation: Integrate out the heavy sector and match the light spectrum, gauge/Higgs couplings, Yukawas and Majorana data.
blockers.falsifier: A mirror remains light, an observed representation is absent, or matching violates measured coupling and heavy-boson bounds.
blockers.externalInputBoundary: Selected vacuum, thresholds and measured matching inputs.

blockers.firstMissingDatum: Canonical normalized physical probes in the matched theory.
blockers.smallestResolvingCalculation: Compute one renormalized two-by-two spin-two/spin-zero spectral response with its mixing and finite-contact prescription.
blockers.falsifier: The response is rank one, basis arbitrary, nonpositive beyond allowed subtraction, or entirely removable by source redefinition.
blockers.externalInputBoundary: Chosen observable, scheme and experimental channel.

blockers.firstMissingDatum: A microscopic holonomy-to-stress coefficient and a realizable sector preparation.
blockers.smallestResolvingCalculation: Predict and then measure the nuisance-projected transverse amplitude across controlled sectors with independent replication.
blockers.falsifier: Adequately powered data remain in the fixed rank-two plane, or the response does not track the prepared sector.
blockers.conditionalWork: Charged-defect spectrum, power design and platform controls.
blockers.externalInputBoundary: Platform-specific coupling, noise, calibration and replicated data.
